extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate mathematics education researchers and university mathematics instructors (those interested in inquiry-oriented instruction and pedagogical reasoning)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and insights for analyzing and supporting instructors' pedagogical reasoning about inquiry-oriented undergraduate mathematics instruction, especially how talk and facilitation relate to engagement with mathematical content and student reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional triangle vertices
rubrics_metrics.description: Pedagogical reasoning about inquiry-oriented instruction relative to vertices of the instructional triangle (content, students, and instructor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When characterizing or evaluating pedagogical reasoning, attend explicitly to how content, students, and instructor perspectives are considered and related.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task sequences supporting deeper mathematical engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Deeper mathematical engagement in task sequences designed for students supported deeper engagement in students’ mathematical reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design task sequences that require substantive mathematical work; such design choices are linked to richer engagement with students' reasoning during instructor discussions about instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional reasoning accompanied by mathematical or student-based rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasoning about instruction was more frequently accompanied by rationale based in mathematics or students’ reasoning about mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When instructors justify instructional moves, strong justifications reference mathematical structure or evidence from student thinking rather than only generic pedagogical claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitator prompts to adopt a mathematical lens
rubrics_metrics.description: Deeper mathematical engagement was observed when the discussion facilitator prompted participants to engage through a mathematical lens rather than an instructional lens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitators should prompt participants to analyze tasks and student work mathematically (e.g., focus on mathematical structure, representations, or problem-solving moves) to encourage deeper pedagogical reasoning tied to content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place for teacher-centered discourse within inquiry instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Even in inquiry-oriented instruction and other forms of active learning, there is a place for integrating teacher-centered discourse (Rasmussen and Marrongelle 2006).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate instructional designs with flexibility: appropriate integration of teacher-centered talk can complement inquiry-based activities rather than being seen as mutually exclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret instructor self-labels cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructors who describe their instruction as 'lecture' often report utilizing a wide variety of other instructional techniques (Johnson et al. 2018).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on instructors' labels ('lecture' vs. 'inquiry') when assessing practice; examine observed techniques and interactions for a fuller picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow multiple codes per turn in discourse analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Each turn of talk could receive more than one code, so the percentages in Fig. 4 sum to over 100%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When coding conversational data about instruction, permit multiple overlapping codes per turn; interpret aggregated percentages accordingly (they may exceed 100%).

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Other' category examples in coding
rubrics_metrics.description: Turns of talk coded as 'Other' included introductions, logistics ('Does everyone have a handout?'), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define and document what constitutes the 'Other' code in discourse analyses to make clear which non-content/ non-pedagogical interactions are aggregated there.
